Q: Google sheets formatting percentages wrong A:

Not sure if this answers the question but from Google Sheets manual:

Format > Number > Custom number formatting

  • @ % - as a string this will display 32.6 % and 32.6 when editing a cell.

  • ##.# \% - as a number this will display 32.6 % and 3260% when editing a cell.

Q: Separating values within string A:

You can create your own customized Community Connector that will do this. In the connector code, this field will have to be parsed into separate fields. You can use split() to do that.

Q: Ttk Entry widget's validation option filters ok for interactive text entry, but not for cut/paste - how to fix? A:

After playing around some more, this seems to work just fine:

def validate_input(self, P, S):
    if '$' in S:
        return False
    return True

def on_invalid_input(self, P, S):
    self.entry.delete(0, tk.END)
    self.entry.insert(0, P.replace('$', ''))

vcmd = (root.register(validate_input), '%P', '%S')
ivcmd = (root.register(on_invalid_input), '%P', '%S')

entry = ttk.Entry(root, 
                  validate='key',
                  validatecommand=vcmd,
                  invalidcommand=ivcmd,
                  **entry_kwargs
                  )

Apparently you need to go through the motions of validate_input() returning a False, and then the Entry's invalidcommand fires. It works for manual entry or cut/paste, at the risk of being somewhat redundant in the manual entry case.

(Note that the partial code is pulled from a class, whence the self)

Q: How to Show Whether a Task Row Is Currently Locked by a Worker A:

AFAIK you cannot use pg_locks view to check all row locks for a given table:

https://postgrespro.com/community/books/internals says

In PostgreSQL the information on whether a particular row is locked is kept only

in the header of its current heap tuple. Row-level locks are virtually attributes in

heap pages rather than actual locks, and they are not reflected in RAM in any way

But there is a expensive way to do it with pgrowlocks which is a standard extension:

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgrowlocks.html

Actually there is cheap way to check if a row is already locked for update with FOR UPDATE NOWAIT clause.

Example:

Session 1:

*# begin;
BEGIN
# update t set x=3 where x=1;
UPDATE 1
*#

Session 2:

# begin;
BEGIN
*# select x from t where x=1 for update nowait;
ERROR:  could not obtain lock on row in relation "t"
!#
